> This appendix generates the pre-registration of `fba-allergy-online-02`, the
large-scale online replication of @beesley2011, in the Psychological Research
Preregistration-Quantitative (PRP-QUANT) Template, version 4 [@prpquant2026],
with the `{preregr}` package.

The form is structured according to the PreReg web form of the template
(<https://apps.leibniz-psychology.org/prp-quant/>) and rebuilt for `{preregr}`.
This notebook exports its result to the `outputs/` folder: once as a PDF and
once as a state file of the web form (`A1-replication-prereg-zpid.rds`), which
the web form can load via its *Import previous state* functionality, to be
checked there and submitted to PreReg, which is the registry of the Leibniz
Institute for Psychology (ZPID).

::: {.callout-tip title="None of the numbers is typed in by hand"}
Sample sizes, significance thresholds and the decision tree are read from the
design that was exported by the power analysis notebook
(`03-replication-power.qmd`) and the exclusion rules come from the provenance
record of the pilot's `{catlasr}` data bundle, apart from the two rules that
`fba-allergy-online-02` rewords. The registration thus cannot drift from the
analyses that justify its contents.
:::

# Specification

Here, I fill the pre-registration form section by section in the collapsed
chunks of R code below. Each item's text is written with `prereg_text()`
function, which fills in the values of the design and joins the lines of every
paragraph. Items marked as not applicable hold the form's not-applicable text,
which the export turns into a ticked *NA* checkbox.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="R code: Pre-registration form"}
### Set-up

```{r}
#| label: replication-prereg-envir
# {preregr} is called with its namespace rather than attached, because
# attaching it masks base::source()
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(gt))

# Search files in relation to the project repository directory, so that the
# code remains renderable no matter where it is called from
REPO <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("CATLAS.Rproj"))
MANUSCRIPT <- "forward-blocking-attention-01"

# Bibliography and citation style, for the references of R1 and the exports
BIB <- file.path(REPO, "common", "references.bib")
CSL <- file.path(REPO, "common", "csl", "apa.csl")

# Formatting, output, effect-size and pre-registration helpers shared by all
# manuscripts, the PRP-QUANT V4 form, and the two-look design of the power
# analysis
source(file.path(REPO, "common", "R", "utils-print.R"))
source(file.path(REPO, "common", "R", "utils-outputs.R"))
source(file.path(REPO, "common", "R", "utils-stats.R"))
source(file.path(REPO, "common", "R", "utils-prereg.R"))
source(file.path(REPO, "common", "R", "prereg-prpquant-v4.R"))
source(file.path(REPO, "manuscripts", MANUSCRIPT, "R", "03-replication-power.R"))

# The design exported by the power analysis notebook, and the pilot estimates
# and attrition funnel exported by the feasibility notebook
design <- read_output("03-replication-design.rds", MANUSCRIPT)
estimates <- read_output("02-feasibility-estimates.rds", MANUSCRIPT)
funnel <- read_output("02-feasibility-funnel.rds", MANUSCRIPT)

# The exclusion rules, verbatim from the provenance record of the pilot's naive
# data bundle
rules_pilot <- catlasr::provenance(
  catlasr::read_private_rds("fba-allergy-online-01/naive.rds")
)$exclusions

# The rules are messaged by {preregr} only when an item fails validation
preregr::opts$set(silent = TRUE)

# Items marked as not applicable hold this text
NA_TEXT <- "Not applicable."

# Start the pre-registration
fba_allergy_online_02 <- preregr::prereg_initialize(form_prpquant_v4(NA_TEXT))
```

```{r}
#| label: replication-prereg-values
# Values of the design, named as in the power analysis notebook
alpha_test <- design$alpha_test
alpha1 <- design$alpha1
scenarios <- design$scenarios
sizes <- design$sizes
n1_recruit <- design$n1_recruit
n1_min <- design$n1_min
n1_planned <- design$n1_planned
planned <- design$planned
by_retention <- design$by_retention
retention_assumed <- design$retention_assumed
stopifnot(
  identical(names(scenarios), c("worst", "realistic", "best")),
  planned$n1 == n1_planned
)

# The pilot: effect sizes by set and index, and the attrition funnel
sets <- c(
  full    = "1 · Full sample",
  learned = "2 · Learned",
  naive   = "3 · Naive"
)
d_bi2 <- purrr::map_dbl(sets, \(s) pick_estimate(estimates, s, "bi_confidence"))
d_bi3 <- purrr::map_dbl(sets, \(s) pick_estimate(estimates, s, "bi_choice"))
pilot_records <- funnel$Total[1L]
pilot_naive <- funnel$Total[nrow(funnel)]
labels_records <- funnel$LABELS[1L]
labels_naive <- funnel$LABELS[nrow(funnel)]

# BI3 is tested at the same looks against the same boundaries as BI2
design_planned <- design_topup(
  n1_planned,
  planned$n2,
  alpha_test,
  "fixed",
  alpha1
)
bi3_look1 <- purrr::map_dbl(
  round(d_bi3, 2),
  \(d) power_topup(design_planned, planned$n2, d)[["look1"]]
)

# Expected precision at look 1: the 90% CI of d_z at the planned sample, if the
# true effect equals the Realistic scenario
ci_realistic <- ci_d_one_sample(
  t = scenarios[["realistic"]] * sqrt(n1_planned),
  n = n1_planned,
  level = 1 - design$alpha_ci
)

# The top-up rule at the four illustrated retention rates
illustration <- with(
  by_retention,
  paste0(
    sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * retention), " retention: ",
    n1, " at look 1, ", n2, " at look 2 (", recruit_total,
    " recruited in total), nominal one-sided *p* < ", print_alpha(p2, 4L)
  )
)

# Versions of the software the registration names. For {catlasr}, the
# registered release, also when its development version (".9000") is installed
version_catlasr <- sub(
  "\\.9[0-9]{3}$",
  "",
  as.character(utils::packageVersion("catlasr"))
)
version_rpact <- as.character(utils::packageVersion("rpact"))

# The contributors, as entered in the contributor fields of the web form
contributors <- tibble::tibble(
  name        = "Josef Mana",
  affiliation = "Institute of Psychology of the Czech Academy of Sciences",
  department  = "The Department of Cognitive Psychology",
  orcid       = "0000-0002-7817-3978",
  role        = "Author(s) / Creator(s)"
)
```

### Abstract (A)

```{r}
#| label: replication-prereg-section-a
fba_allergy_online_02 <- preregr::prereg_specify(
  fba_allergy_online_02,

  # Project description
  A1 = prereg_text("
    **Background.** In forward blocking, a cue is learned about less when
    presented with another cue that already predicts the outcome. In the
    three-stage design of @beesley2011, blocked cues are also learned about
    less when paired with new outcomes, indicating selective inattention to
    the blocked cues.

    **Objectives.** To replicate the three-stage blocking effect in a large
    online sample and to select the blocking index for the extension study to
    follow.

    **Participants.** Students of the LABELS participant pool of Charles
    University, tested online. Recruitment of {{n1_recruit}} participants at
    look 1, aiming at {{n1_planned}} (at least {{n1_min}}) in the primary
    analysis set, with a pre-registered top-up at look 2 (see M3).

    **Method.** A within-participant three-stage modified allergist task.
    Blocking is tested by one-sided one-sample *t*-tests of the original index
    of @beesley2011 and of an alternative choice-based index, in a two-look
    group-sequential design.
  "),

  # Keywords
  A2 = prereg_text("
    associative learning, cue competition, learned attention, contingency
    learning, forward blocking, allergist task
  "),

  # Research area
  A3 = "Cognitive psychology"
)
```

### Introduction (I)

```{r}
#| label: replication-prereg-section-i
fba_allergy_online_02 <- preregr::prereg_specify(
  fba_allergy_online_02,

  # Theoretical background
  I1 = prereg_text("
    Forward blocking refers to the attenuation of learning about a cue-outcome
    relationship when the cue is accompanied by another cue that has already
    been established to predict the same outcome [@kamin1969; @dickinson1984;
    @shanks1985]. Although under certain experimental conditions, blocking
    follows from error-driven learning alone [@rescorla1972], eye-tracking and
    behavioural studies suggest that it is often accompanied by learned
    inattention to the blocked cue [@kruschke2005; @lepelley2007; @beesley2011].
    
    Learned-attention models explain it either by rapid attentional shifts or by
    attentional competition [@kruschke2001]. @paskewitz2020 proposed a design
    that could adjudicate between these two explanations, which is yet to be
    experimentally tested. Whereas in the canonical two-stage design, blocking
    can be explained without any attentional mechanism [@sewell2012], in the
    three-stage design of @lepelley2007 and @beesley2011, blocked and control
    cues are paired with new outcomes in a third stage, in the absence of their
    former competitors, so that a deficit in learning about the blocked cue must
    generalise beyond its original association. This design thus requires an
    attentional mechanism [@paskewitz2020] and forms the basis of the planned
    extension study.

    However, blocking may not as reliable as its standing in the literature
    suggests. @maes2016 failed to detect it in fifteen replications of published
    rodent paradigms. The extension of the three-stage design aim at in this
    study is therefore preceded by a replication of its behavioural result in
    the setting in which the extension will run, i.e., an online experiment. A
    pilot study of the present procedure (`fba-allergy-online-01`, see M2) found
    effects in the predicted direction, but was too imprecise to decide about
    its reliability.
  "),

  # Objectives and research questions
  I2 = prereg_text("
    The study has two objectives:

    1. To replicate the blocking effect of @beesley2011, measured by their
    confidence-weighted index on the first test block, in a large online
    sample of participants without prior knowledge of the paradigm.

    2. To select the blocking index for the extension study
    (`fba-allergy-online-03`), with options being the original
    confidence-weighted index or an alternative choice-based index used by the
    simulations of @paskewitz2020.

    The study also provides effect size estimates for the power analysis of the
    extension study.
  "),

  # Hypotheses
  I3 = prereg_text("
    Both hypotheses are tested in the Naive set (i.e., participants showing
    sufficient learning who are unfamiliar with the study design, see AP1),
    one-sided, in the direction of blocking.

    - **H1** (decides the replication). The mean of BI~2~, the
      confidence-weighted blocking index of @beesley2011 on the first test
      block, is greater than zero.

    - **H2** (decides the index of `fba-allergy-online-03`; has no bearing on
      the replication). The mean of BI~3~, the choice-based blocking index of
      @paskewitz2020 over all six test blocks, is greater than zero.

    Both indices are defined in M12. Positive values of either index indicate
    blocking, i.e., test choices of the outcome paired in Stage 3 with the
    control rather than with the blocked cue.
  "),

  # Purely exploratory study
  I3_1 = "No",

  # Exploratory questions
  I4 = prereg_text("
    The test stage is repeated six times, compared to a single block in
    @beesley2011, which allows asking how stable blocking is across the test
    stage (E4) and how reliably the indices measure it (E2 and E3). Indices that
    are robust at the group level may still rank participants unreliably [the
    reliability paradox, @hedge2018], which lowers precision of any later
    correlation estimates of blocking as a trait with other trait-like variables
    (e.g., correlating a behavioural with eye-tracking blocking index by
    @beesley2011).

    - **E1.** Given the sample reached, what are the probabilities of a sign
      error and the expected exaggeration of a significant estimate
      [@gelman2014] under each effect size scenario of M3.2?

    - **E2.** How strongly are BI~2~ and BI~3~ correlated across participants?

    - **E3a.** How strongly are per-block indices correlated between test
      blocks and does the learning check raise these correlations?

    - **E3b.** What is the test-retest reliability (ICC) of the per-block
      indices?

    - **E4a.** Does blocking change across the six test blocks, on average and
      by participant (frequentist mixed models)?

    - **E4b.** If blocking drifts, does it drift towards zero fast enough to
      matter in practice (Bayesian mixed models)?
  ")
)
```

### Method, data collection (M1 to M8)

```{r}
#| label: replication-prereg-section-md
fba_allergy_online_02 <- preregr::prereg_specify(
  fba_allergy_online_02,

  # Time point of registration
  M1 = "Registration before creation/collection of data",

  # Pre-existing data
  M1_1 = NA_TEXT,

  # Piloting
  M2 = prereg_text("
    The procedure of this study was piloted in `fba-allergy-online-01`, run
    online via JATOS on <https://mindprobe.eu> between 9 and 26 June 2026, with
    participants recruited from the LABELS pool and among personal contacts.
    Out of {{pilot_records}} participant records, {{pilot_naive}} reached the
    Naive set. The pilot was analysed in full (descriptive statistics, learning
    check, both blocking indices, stability across test blocks) to estimate the
    effect sizes of both indices, the retention and the yield of every exclusion
    rule and to detect technical problems of the experiment.

    The pilot estimated *d*~z~ = {{print_d(d_bi2[['full']])}} for BI~2~ in the
    Full sample, {{print_d(d_bi2[['learned']])}} in the Learned set and
    {{print_d(d_bi2[['naive']])}} in the Naive set, which inspire the
    *Realistic* and *Worst* scenarios of M3.2, and *d*~z~ =
    {{print_d(d_bi3[['full']])}}, {{print_d(d_bi3[['learned']])}} and
    {{print_d(d_bi3[['naive']])}} for BI~3~. Its retention sets the assumed
    retention of M3.2.

    The pilot's participants are not eligible for this study, and its data are
    never pooled with this study's data. Its analyses are documented in the
    notebook *2 · Feasibility Study* (`02-feasibility-study.qmd`) of the
    `CATLAS` repository.
  "),

  # Planned sample size
  M3_sample_size = prereg_text("
    Sample sizes refer to the Naive set (see AP1), unless stated otherwise.

    **Look 1.** {{n1_recruit}} participants are recruited, aiming at
    {{n1_planned}} in the Naive set at the assumed retention of
    {{sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * retention_assumed)}}, and analysed provided at
    least {{n1_min}} reach the set given exclusion criteria (see M3.3).

    **Look 2** (only if neither index detects blocking at look 1, see M3.3 and
    AP10). The Naive set is brought to the sample *n*~2~ set by the rule of
    M3.3: {{planned$n2}} participants at the assumed
    {{sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * retention_assumed)}} retention, about
    {{planned$recruit_total}} recruited in total. The rule at the four
    retention rates illustrated in the power analysis:

    {{paste0('- ', illustration, collapse = '\n')}}
  "),

  # Sample size justification
  M3_justification = prereg_text("
    **Effect size scenarios.** Sample sizes are planned for BI~2~ (H1) in the
    Naive set, for a one-sided one-sample *t*-test at &alpha; =
    {{print_alpha(alpha_test, 2L)}}, under three scenarios of the true
    standardised mean *d*~z~: *Best* [{{print_d(scenarios[['best']])}},
    @beesley2011], *Realistic* ({{print_d(scenarios[['realistic']])}}, the
    pilot's Full sample) and *Worst* ({{print_d(scenarios[['worst']])}}, the
    pilot's Naive set). A single test needs
    {{pick_size(sizes, 'realistic', 0.90)}} participants for 90% power under the
    *Realistic* scenario and {{n1_planned}} for 95%.

    **Retention.** The retention, i.e., the share of recruited participants
    who reach the final Naive set, is assumed to be
    {{sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * retention_assumed)}}. In the pilot study, it was
    {{print_n_pct(pilot_naive, pilot_records)}} overall and
    {{print_n_pct(labels_naive, labels_records)}} among participants of the
    LABELS pool.

    **Design.** The study is a two-look group-sequential design [@wassmer2025],
    planned according to design calculations using the `rpact` R package
    [@wassmer2026] with *t*-based power (see M3.3 for the looks specification).
    With {{n1_planned}} participants, look 1 has
    {{print_power(planned$look1_realistic)}} power under the *Realistic* and
    {{print_power(planned$look1_worst)}} under the *Worst* scenario. Look 2 is
    sized for 80% overall power across both looks under the *Worst* scenario.

    **BI~3~** (H2) is tested at the same looks against the same boundaries.
    With {{n1_planned}} participants at look 1, its power is
    {{print_power(bi3_look1[['full']])}} if its true effect equals the pilot's
    Full sample estimate (*d*~z~ = {{print_d(d_bi3[['full']])}}) and
    {{print_power(bi3_look1[['learned']])}} if it equals the Learned set
    estimate (*d*~z~ = {{print_d(d_bi3[['learned']])}}).

    **Precision.** If the true effect equals the *Realistic* scenario, the 90%
    confidence interval of *d*~z~ at {{n1_planned}} participants is expected to
    be {{print_ci(ci_realistic[1L], ci_realistic[2L])}}.

    The power analysis is documented in the notebook *3 · Experiment 1: Power
    Analysis* (`03-replication-power.qmd`) of the `CATLAS` repository.
  "),

  # Stopping rule
  M3_stopping_rule = prereg_text("
    **Look 1** is the replication proper. Recruitment closes once {{n1_recruit}}
    participants have started the experiment ({{n1_planned}} /
    {{retention_assumed}}), and the data are analysed once recruitment has
    closed, provided at least {{n1_min}} of them reach the final Naive set. If
    fewer participants do, recruitment continues in batches sized to reach
    {{n1_planned}} at the retention observed so far, until at least {{n1_min}}
    reach the Naive set. Look 1 spends a fixed one-sided &alpha;~1~ =
    {{print_alpha(alpha1)}}.

    **Look 2** takes place if and only if neither BI~2~ nor BI~3~ detects
    blocking at look 1 (see AP10). It brings the Naive set to the smallest
    sample *n*~2~ that gives the design 80% overall power across both looks
    under the *Worst* scenario, given the look-1 sample *n*~1~ actually reached.
    The number of participants recruited for look 2 assumes the retention
    observed at look 1. If fewer than *n*~2~ then reach the Naive set,
    recruitment continues in batches, as at look 1. Only these outcome-blind
    quantities, i.e., the sample reached and the retention, enter the sampling
    rule; the look-1 blocking estimates never do. At the assumed retention,
    look 2 rejects the null hypothesis at a nominal one-sided *p* <
    {{print_alpha(planned$p2, 4L)}} (see M3.1 for other retention rates).

    **Cap on look 2.** If the rule specified above asks for more participants
    than the LABELS pool can supply in one semester, look 2 stops at the largest
    available sample size, and the power it achieves is reported.

    **Critical values** are recomputed for the samples actually reached at each
    look, keeping &alpha;~1~ = {{print_alpha(alpha1)}} and the overall &alpha;
    = {{print_alpha(alpha_test, 2L)}}.

    **No other look** at either blocking index is planned. Attrition, completion
    time and the yield of the learning check are monitored during data collection
    (see M7).
  "),

  # Population of interest
  M4_population = "University students",

  # Recruitment method
  M4_recruitment = prereg_text("
    The LABELS participant pool of Charles University, Prague
    (<https://labels.ff.cuni.cz/studenti>), among students who did not take
    part in the pilot `fba-allergy-online-01`. Participants are tested online
    via JATOS (<https://www.jatos.org>) on <https://mindprobe.eu>, in the Czech
    version of the experiment. Recruitment proceeds in batches, opened in the
    order set by the sampling rules of M3.3. No batch of look 2 opens before
    the look-1 analysis is complete.
  "),

  # Planned participant characteristics
  M4_characteristics = prereg_text("
    Charles University students, primarily of Czech nationality, 18–35 years
    old, with an expected predominance of women. Each participant must be at
    least 18 years of age and run the experiment on a laptop or desktop
    computer. No participant characteristics are targeted.
  "),

  # Quota or stratification sampling
  M4_quotas = NA_TEXT,

  # Compensation
  M4_compensation = prereg_text("
    Partial credit for the course \"Vybraná témata z psychologie a
    psycholingvistiky\" (ABO700887) at Charles University, the same for every
    participant. Participation is confirmed by a screenshot of the farewell
    screen or by the e-mail address that participants may enter after giving
    consent. The address is optional (participants who prefer to stay anonymous
    enter \"x\"), is used solely for the credit, is separated from the responses
    when the data are downloaded, and is deleted once LABELS has confirmed
    participation.
  "),

  # Drop-out
  M5 = prereg_text("
    Participants who leave before completing the first test block are excluded
    (rule 3 of AP1) and not replaced. Participants who leave later keep the test
    blocks they completed, with BI~2~ using their first test block only and
    BI~3~ all the test blocks present (see AP5).
  "),

  # Masking
  M6 = prereg_text("
    Participants are not informed of the hypotheses. The task is presented as
    learning which side effects vitamin pills cause in fictitious patients. All
    conditions are within participants, so there is no allocation to conceal.
    The experiment runs online without an experimenter. The learning check (rule
    4 of AP1) uses learning-stage data only and the free-text debriefing answers
    (rule 5) are coded from a file that holds only the participant identifiers
    and the debriefing answers (see AP4), before any blocking index is
    computed, so that both rules are blind to the test data.
  "),

  # Ensuring quality during data collection
  M7 = prereg_text("
    During data collection, only attrition, completion time and the yield of the
    learning check are monitored, to detect technical problems. Neither index is
    computed before the analysis of a look. A technical failure that invalidates
    data (e.g., lost uploads) may stop data collection until it is fixed; any
    stop is reported with its reason. Any look at either index outside the looks
    of M3.3 is a deviation from this protocol.
  ")
)
```

---

### Method, conditions and design (M9 to M18)

```{r}
#| label: replication-prereg-section-mc
fba_allergy_online_02 <- preregr::prereg_specify(
  fba_allergy_online_02,

  # Research method
  M9 = "Experiment",
  M9_1 = "Design with repeated measures (only \"within-subject\" variables)",
  M9_1_1 = prereg_text("
    An experimental, cross-sectional study with a single group and a
    within-participant three-stage forward blocking design [@lepelley2007;
    @beesley2011], specified as the `three-stage-replication` design of
    `catlasr` and illustrated in Table 1 of the manuscript. Each stage consists
    of blocks of eight trial types.

    - **Stage 1** (elemental training): four blocking cues and four filler cues,
      each paired with one of two outcomes (o1, o2).

    - **Stage 2** (compound training): each blocking cue in compound with a new
      cue (the blocked cues), and four compounds of two new cues (one of them a
      control cue), paired with o1 or o2.

    - **Stage 3** (novel learning): four compounds of one blocked and one
      control cue, paired with two new outcomes (o3, o4), and four filler
      compounds of new cues.

    - **Test**: eight pairs of one blocked and one control cue that were paired
      with different outcomes in Stage 3. Blocking predicts preference for the
      choice of the control cue's outcome.

    The factor of interest, cue status (blocked or control), is thus manipulated
    within participants and test pairs.
  "),

  # Multilevel structure
  M10 = prereg_text("
    Trial-level responses are nested within crossed by-participant and
    by-test-pair clusters. The confirmatory tests (AP8) use one value of each
    index per participant; the exploratory mixed models (E4a, E4b) model the
    trial level.
  "),

  # Randomisation
  M11 = prereg_text("
    Independently for each participant, the 28 cue roles are randomly assigned
    the names of 28 fictitious chemicals, and the four outcomes are randomly
    assigned the four side effects (dizziness, itchiness, headache, nausea).
    Within every block, the order of the eight trial types is randomised, with
    the constraint that no trial type repeats across a block boundary. The
    left-right order of the two cues of a compound is counterbalanced across the
    blocks of Stages 2 and 3 and of the test stage. The screen position of the
    outcomes is fixed (o1 and o3 left, o2 and o4 right).
  "),

  # Variables of the confirmatory analyses
  M12 = prereg_text("
    **Dependent variables.** On every test trial, the outcome chosen (one of the
    two Stage 3 outcomes) and the confidence in the choice (1, *Not confident at
    all*, to 10, *Very confident*). From these, the signed confidence of a trial
    is the confidence if the participant chose the outcome paired in Stage 3
    with the control cue of the pair, and minus the confidence otherwise.

    - **BI~2~** [@beesley2011]: the mean signed confidence over the answered
      trials of the first test block, i.e., of 8 trials (from −10 to 10;
      `catlasr::index_blocking(blocks = 1)`, column `bi_confidence`). It is the
      index of H1.

    - **BI~3~** [@paskewitz2020]: over the answered trials of all six test
      blocks, i.e., of up to 48 trials, the sum across the eight test pairs of
      the proportion of choices of the control cue's outcome, minus one half
      per pair (from −4 to 4; `catlasr::index_blocking(blocks = NULL)`, column
      `bi_choice`). It is the index of H2.

    **Independent variable.** Cue status (blocked or control), manipulated
    within participants (M9.1.1); the indices contrast the two.
  "),

  # Other variables
  M13 = prereg_text("
    Accuracy and response times of the learning trials (the learning check of
    AP1), response times of the test trials, the two debriefing answers and
    whether the debriefing timed out (AP1, rule 5), age and sex (sample
    description only), and the duration of the run. An optional free-text
    comment at the end of the debriefing is neither imported nor analysed.
    No covariates enter the confirmatory analyses.
  "),

  # Exhaustiveness of variables
  M14 = prereg_text(
    "All variables of the planned study are outlined here and their roles are
    clearly defined. We are aware that any changes to the variables and their
    defined roles is a deviation from this preregistration and must be reported
    in the article."
  ),

  # Collection mode
  M15 = prereg_text(
    "Instrumental measurements (e.g., response times, eye tracking, motion
    tracking, EEG, ECG, pulse sensor, breathing, (f)MRI, body dimensions);
    Surveys (e.g., interviews, questionnaires)"
  ),

  # Study materials
  M16 = prereg_text("
    The experiment is programmed in jsPsych (PD5). Every build of it lives in
    one folder of the `catlaslab` repository,
    `studies/forward-blocking-attention-01/fba-allergy-online/`, and builds are
    told apart by release tags, each with the JATOS study archive (`.jzip`) as
    deployed attached. This study runs the release `fba-allergy-online-02`; the
    pilot ran `fba-allergy-online-01`. The cue names follow the fictitious
    chemicals of @lepelley2007, adapted to Czech. Every trial shows the cue
    names with a flask icon at the top of the screen, the question which
    reaction the patient will experience, and two images of the patient (Mr X in
    Stages 1 and 2, Mr Y in Stage 3 and the test stage), each showing one side
    effect.
  "),

  # Study procedures
  M17 = prereg_text("
    The procedure follows @beesley2011, a variant of the allergist task
    [@dickinson1996; @lochmann2003]. A browser check first turns away devices
    whose browser reports itself as mobile (mostly phones). A welcome screen,
    which asks participants to reserve about 25 to 30 minutes, a stable
    internet connection and a quiet environment, and four screens of study
    information precede the informed consent. Declining consent ends the
    experiment and deletes the data recorded so far. Participants may then
    enter an e-mail address for the course credit (M4.5), state their sex and
    age (both required, with no answer preselected), and read the instructions,
    which include animated tutorials and requests not to take notes and to
    focus on correct rather than fast responses. Stage 1 has 10
    blocks (80 trials), Stage 2 has 8 blocks (64 trials), Stage 3 has 6 blocks
    (48 trials) and the test stage has 6 blocks (48 trials). On every trial,
    participants click the image of the side effect they predict and confirm
    with an OK button. In Stages 1–3, the words *Correct* (green) or *Wrong*
    (red) and a frame around the correct image follow every response for 1.5
    seconds. In the test stage, there is no feedback and every choice is
    followed by the confidence rating. Stage 3 introduces a new patient, with
    a new instruction text. A learning trial without a response ends after 60
    seconds. A test trial ends as unanswered after 60 seconds unless both the
    choice and the confidence rating are given. Instruction screens end after
    180 seconds and the consent screen has no time limit. The experiment ends
    with the debriefing questions of AP1 (rule 5), whose screen also ends after
    180 seconds, an optional comment, and a farewell screen that serves as the
    confirmation of participation (M4.5).
  "),

  # Other information
  M18 = prereg_text("
    The power analysis behind M3 is documented in the notebook
    *3 · Experiment 1: Power Analysis* (`03-replication-power.qmd`) of the
    `CATLAS` repository, and the pilot behind it in *2 · Feasibility Study*
    (`02-feasibility-study.qmd`).
  ")
)
```

---

### Analysis plan (AP)

```{r}
#| label: replication-prereg-section-ap
# Labels of the five exclusion rules, as in the feasibility notebook, in the
# order they are applied in `fba-allergy-online-02`. Declining consent newly
# deletes the run's data (starting from `catlaslab@fba-allergy-online-02`), so
# the consent rule needs to come first; in second place it would never fire,
# because every declined run would already count as one without jsPsych data.
rule_labels <- c(
  declined_consent                   = "Declined consent",
  no_jspsych_data                    = "No jsPsych data",
  incomplete_run                     = "Incomplete run",
  learning_not_reliably_above_chance = "Insufficient learning",
  prior_knowledge_reported           = "Prior knowledge"
)

# Rules 1 and 5 are reworded for `fba-allergy-online-02`: declining deletes the
# data recorded so far and the debriefing has two parts and a time limit. Rules
# 2 to 4 are the same as in the pilot. The data set script of
# `fba-allergy-online-02` (`{catlasr}`, `data-raw/fba-allergy-online-02.R`)
# records all five verbatim.
rule_declined_consent <- prereg_text("
  The participant declined on the informed-consent screen. Declining ends the
  experiment and deletes the data recorded so far, so that JATOS keeps only
  the study result, in the state ABORTED.
")

rule_prior_knowledge <- prereg_text("
  The participant answered yes to the debriefing question \"Before today,
  have you taken part in an experiment in which you predicted reactions from
  foods or medicines?\", their answer to the debriefing question \"Did you
  know or guess what this study tested? If so, describe it.\" was coded as
  describing blocking, or the debriefing screen timed out or was not reached.
  An answer describes blocking if it states that learning about a cue is
  reduced when the cue is presented together with a cue that already predicts
  the outcome, or if it names blocking, cue competition or learned
  (in)attention. Answers that describe only the surface of the task
  (predicting side effects, memory, attention or learning in general) do not.
  The answers are coded before any blocking index is computed.
")

revised_02 <- c(
  declined_consent = rule_declined_consent,
  prior_knowledge_reported = rule_prior_knowledge
)

# The pilot's records in the order of fba-allergy-online-02
rules_pilot_02 <- rules_pilot[
  match(names(rule_labels), purrr::map_chr(rules_pilot, "rule"))
]

rules_02 <- write_prereg_rules(
  rules_pilot_02,
  rule_labels,
  revised = revised_02
)

# The wording of every rule, named by rule, saved in the export below
rule_texts <- purrr::map_chr(rules_pilot_02, "description")
names(rule_texts) <- names(rule_labels)
rule_texts[names(revised_02)] <- revised_02

decisions_02 <- write_prereg_decisions(design$decisions, design$thresholds)

fba_allergy_online_02 <- preregr::prereg_specify(
  fba_allergy_online_02,

  # Exclusion of participants
  AP1 = prereg_text("
    **Inclusion criteria for data collection.** Students of the LABELS pool
    (M4.2) who are at least 18 years old, did not take part in the pilot
    `fba-allergy-online-01`, and run the experiment on a laptop or desktop
    computer.

    **Exclusion criteria.** Participants are excluded by the following rules,
    applied in the order listed. An excluded participant is counted under the
    first rule that removes them. Rules 2–4 are worded verbatim as in the
    provenance record of the pilot's data. Rule 1 is reworded because declining
    consent now deletes the data recorded until that point and it is applied
    first so that a declined run is not counted under rule 2. Rule 5 is reworded
    for the new debriefing question.

    {{paste(rules_02, collapse = '\n')}}

    The debriefing questions of rule 5 are shown in Czech: \"Účastnil/a jste
    se již před dneškem experimentu, ve kterém jste předpovídal/a reakce na
    potraviny nebo léky?\" (*Ano* / *Ne*) and \"Věděl/a jste nebo tušil/a,
    co tato studie zkoumala? Pokud ano, popište to.\" Both are compulsory: the
    screen cannot be left before the first is answered and the second holds
    text.

    The rules define three nested analysis sets: the **Full sample** (after
    rules 1–3), the **Learned set** (after rules 1–4) and the **Naive
    set** (after rules 1–5). The Naive set is the primary analysis set and
    alone tests H1 and H2. The other two serve the sensitivity analyses of
    AP8. Rules 4 and 5 are blind to the test data (see M6).

    **Outliers.** No participant is excluded as an outlier on any variable. An
    excluded participant is excluded from all analyses of the sets that the
    rule removes them from.
  "),

  # Exclusion of trials
  AP2 = prereg_text("
    Only timed-out trials, i.e., trials without a response within 60 seconds,
    are excluded (see AP5). No trials are excluded for their response times.
  "),

  # Exhaustiveness of exclusion criteria
  AP3 = "All exclusion criteria (on the participant and trial/item level) that are currently planned are listed above.",

  # Preprocessing and quality control during analyses
  AP4 = prereg_text("
    The JATOS study results are imported, validated and anonymised with the
    `catlasr` R package (PD8), and downloaded with `pull_jatos_batches()`.
    During the experiment, every trial is streamed to JATOS upon its end and, at
    the end of a run, the complete jsPsych data are also uploaded as the result
    file `jspsych-data.json` (`result_file = \"jspsych-data.json\"`). For every
    study result (i.e., run), the result file is read where it exists and the
    streamed data only where it does not (unfinished runs, failed uploads) or
    cannot be parsed. The two are never combined and the source of every study
    result is recorded (as `data_source`) and reported. Before any
    exclusion, the JATOS identifiers are replaced by random six-digit
    participant IDs (via `update_id_key()`), whose key is kept in a private
    folder. The e-mail addresses are kept apart from the responses (M4.5).

    Data bundle validation (via `validate_fba_rawdata()`) must pass before any
    analysis. The exclusion rules of AP1 are recorded in the provenance record
    of the data set with the `record_exclusion()` function, in the order they
    are applied. The learning check of rule 4 is computed with
    `test_learning(alpha = 0.10)` and `screen_learning(rule = \"any\")`. For
    rule 5, `write_debrief_coding()` writes a coding file that contains only the
    participant IDs and the debriefing answers, and `read_debrief_coding()`
    reads the codes back; the data import does not proceed until every answer is
    coded. Test trials are scored with `score_blocking()`, which signs every
    answered trial by whether its choice is consistent with blocking, and the
    indices of M12 are computed per participant with `index_blocking()`: BI~2~
    on the first test block, BI~3~ over all test blocks, and both per test
    block (`by_block = TRUE`) for the exploratory analyses. The indices are not
    screened for outliers, transformed or winsorised.
  "),

  # Missing data
  AP5 = prereg_text("
    **Definition.** A learning trial without a response ends after 60 seconds,
    and so does a test trial in which the choice and the confidence rating are
    not both given. Timed-out trials have no response and enter neither the
    learning check (rule 4 of AP1) nor the calculation of the blocking indices,
    which average over answered trials only. A participant's BI~2~ is missing
    if every trial of the first test block timed out and their BI~3~ if a given
    test pair has no answered trial. Both debriefing questions, upon which
    prior knowledge of the design is established, are compulsory, but the
    debriefing screen ends after 180 seconds. A participant whose debriefing
    timed out or was not reached is excluded from the Naive set by rule 5 of
    AP1.

    **Handling.** A participant whose BI~2~ is missing is left out of the test
    of H1, and a participant whose BI~3~ is missing is left out of the test of
    H2 (case-wise deletion per analysis). Missing data are not imputed.

    **Missingness mechanism.** Whether trials are missing at random is not
    tested. The number of timed-out trials and of participants left out is
    reported.
  "),

  # Reliability
  AP6 = prereg_text("
    The reliability of the indices across the six test blocks is estimated in
    the exploratory analyses E3a and E3b (AP11). It does not enter the
    confirmatory analyses.
  "),

  # Descriptive statistics
  AP7 = prereg_text("
    For the recruited sample: the number of participants removed by each
    exclusion rule; the age and sex of every analysis set, in aggregate only;
    the duration of the run. For the learning stages: the accuracy per stage and
    block, by cue type (learning curves). For each index and analysis set: the
    mean and standard deviation (`aggregate_blocking()`), the 90% confidence
    interval of the mean, and *d*~z~ (mean divided by standard deviation) with
    its exact 90% confidence interval, obtained by inverting the noncentral *t*
    distribution. 90% CIs are selected instead of their more typical 95%
    counterparts because the former align better with the one-sided test applied
    to the data. Finally, per-block means of both indices are plotted across the
    six test blocks.
  "),

  # Statistical models
  AP8 = prereg_text("
    **H1.** One-sided one-sample *t*-test of the per-participant BI~2~
    (`index_blocking()`, AP4) against zero (alternative: mean greater than
    zero), in the Naive set, at each look of M3.3. At look 2, the test uses all
    participants of the Naive set (looks 1 and 2 together) and the critical
    value of the two-look design, computed with `rpact::getAnalysisResults()`
    from the stage-wise sample sizes, means and standard deviations (*t*-based,
    version {{version_rpact}} at registration).

    **H2.** The same test of the per-participant BI~3~, at the same looks and
    boundaries.

    **Correction for multiple testing.** BI~2~ and BI~3~ are not corrected for
    each other, because they decide different questions: only BI~2~ decides the
    replication, only BI~3~'s result decides which index the extension study
    uses (AP10). The two looks are corrected by the &alpha; spending of M3.3.

    **Sensitivity analyses.** *d*~z~ with its 90% confidence interval for both
    indices in the Full sample and in the Learned set. These estimates are
    reported, but do not decide anything.

    **Estimates after look 2.** If the study stops at look 2, the effect is
    reported as the median-unbiased estimate with its confidence interval under
    the stage-wise ordering, which correct the bias of the naive estimate after
    a sequential design, alongside the naive estimate.
  "),

  # Assumption tests
  AP9 = prereg_text("
    **One-sample *t*-tests (H1, H2).** Normality of the per-participant indices
    is not tested; the one-sample *t*-test is applied regardless on the basis
    of the central limit theorem, following established practice of previous
    forward blocking experimental studies. Independence of participants holds
    by design. No transformations or non-parametric alternatives are planned.

    **Mixed models (E4a).** Singular fits are refitted without the correlation
    of the random effects and, if still singular, left out (see AP11).
  "),

  # Inference criteria
  AP10 = prereg_text("
    An index **passes** at a look if its one-sided test rejects the null
    hypothesis of no blocking at the threshold of that look: one-sided *p* <
    {{print_alpha(alpha1)}} at look 1, and below the nominal threshold of the
    recomputed look-2 critical value at look 2 (about
    {{print_alpha(planned$p2, 3L)}} at the
    {{sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * retention_assumed)}} assumed retention, see
    M3.3). H1 and H2 are separate hypotheses without sub-hypotheses. The result
    of BI~2~ alone decides whether the replication succeeds (H1); the result of
    BI~3~ alone decides which index carries on to `fba-allergy-online-03`. The
    decision tree:

    {{paste(decisions_02, collapse = '\n')}}

    A failure at look 2 of both indices ends the online line of studies: the
    next step is a laboratory replication with eye tracking. No smallest effect
    size of interest is defined. The design is planned for 80% overall power at
    *d*~z~ = {{print_d(scenarios[['worst']])}}, the smallest of the scenarios.
    For the extension study, *d*~z~ of the selected index is reported with its
    95% confidence interval, because the extension study tests a two-sided
    hypothesis adjudicating between two competing theories.
  "),

  # Exploratory analyses
  AP11 = prereg_text("
    The following analyses are exploratory and are reported as such, in every
    analysis set.

    - **E1.** A design analysis [@gelman2014] of each index at the sample
      reached, giving the probability of a sign error (Type S) and the expected
      exaggeration ratio (Type M) of a significant estimate under each of the
      three scenarios of M3.2.

    - **E2.** Pearson's correlation of the per-participant BI~2~ and BI~3~,
      with its 95% confidence interval.

    - **E3a.** The 6 × 6 matrices of Pearson's correlations of the per-block
      indices between test blocks, for each index. Higher correlations in the
      Learned and Naive sets than in the Full sample would suggest that the
      learning check raises between-block reliability.

    - **E3b.** Intraclass correlations of the per-block indices across the six
      test blocks, for each index: two-way, consistency, single block (ICC(3,1))
      and mean of six blocks (ICC(3,6)), with 95% confidence intervals.

    - **E4a.** Three nested mixed models of the trial-level data of each index,
      fitted with `{lme4}`: signed confidence (BI~2~) as Gaussian and the
      blocking-consistent choice (BI~3~) as binomial with a logit link, with
      crossed by-participant and by-test-pair random intercepts, and (1) no
      change across test blocks, (2) a common linear drift (test block coded
      0–5), (3) an additional by-participant drift. Singular fits are
      refitted without the correlation of the random effects and, if still
      singular, left out. The models are compared by likelihood-ratio tests and
      AIC.

    - **E4b.** Bayesian versions of the three models, fitted in Stan with weakly
      informative default priors as in `{rstanarm}`, for the choice (binomial,
      logit link) and for the unsigned confidence (ordinal, cumulative logit),
      with linear drift only. If blocking drifts towards zero, the extrapolated
      test block at which the drift line of the choice model crosses zero is
      evaluated by the posterior probability that the slope is greater than
      minus the intercept divided by 9, i.e., that the line crosses zero after
      the 10th test block (and, likewise, after the 6th block, dividing by 5). A
      crossing after the 10th block is taken as practically insignificant drift.
      The slopes of the choice and confidence models are compared.
  "),

  # Other information
  AP12 = "Deviations from this registration are reported and justified in the manuscript."
)
```

### Other information (O) and references (R)

```{r}
#| label: replication-prereg-section-o
fba_allergy_online_02 <- preregr::prereg_specify(
  fba_allergy_online_02,

  # Deviations from the pilot and from the original study
  O1 = prereg_text("
    **Deviations from the pilot `fba-allergy-online-01`.**

    - Data are uploaded in full at the end of the experiment, in addition to
      trial by trial, so that a lost connection no longer loses data.

    - Test trials end after 60 seconds unless both the choice and the confidence
      rating are given; in the pilot, they had no time limit, yet none of its
      test trials took that long.

    - Declining consent aborts the JATOS run, which deletes the data recorded
      so far, and the consent screen has no time limit. In the pilot, a declined
      run kept its data, and the consent screen ended after 120 seconds, after
      which the experiment continued. The consent rule of AP1 is reworded and
      applied first accordingly.

    - The single debriefing question about taking part in a similar experiment
      is replaced by the two compulsory questions of rule 5 of AP1, and the
      exclusion rule is reworded accordingly, with a coding rule for the free
      text. The debriefing screen ends after 180 seconds, and a timed-out
      debriefing excludes the participant from the Naive set.

    - The Naive set is the primary analysis set; in the pilot, it was the
      Learned set. The prior-knowledge exclusion removes participants who may
      answer from what they expect the study to show, which the pilot could not
      afford with its small sample.

    - Participants are recruited from the LABELS pool only (the pilot also
      recruited personal contacts), among students who did not take part in the
      pilot.

    **Deviations from @beesley2011.** The study runs online rather than in the
    laboratory and without eye tracking, in Czech. The test stage is repeated
    six times instead of once. The original index (BI~2~) uses the first test
    block only, so that it remains comparable. Participants who do not learn
    reliably above chance or report prior knowledge are excluded, which
    @beesley2011 did not do.
  ")
)

# The references of every item, generated from the bibliography; specified
# last, so that every citation is included
fba_allergy_online_02 <- preregr::prereg_specify(
  fba_allergy_online_02,
  R1 = prereg_references(fba_allergy_online_02, BIB, CSL)
)
```

# Export

The registration is exported to the manuscript's `outputs/` folder as a PDF
(`A1-replication-prereg.pdf`) and as a state file of the PreReg web form
(`A1-replication-prereg-zpid.rds`). In the state file, the answers are plain
text with the citations resolved. The wording of the exclusion rules of AP1 is
saved on its own (`A1-replication-rules.rds`), named by rule, for the analysis
notebook of `fba-allergy-online-02` to check against the provenance record of
the data set.

```{r}
#| label: replication-prereg-export
outputs <- output_dir(MANUSCRIPT)
dir.create(outputs, showWarnings = FALSE)

prereg_to_pdf(
  fba_allergy_online_02,
  file = file.path(outputs, "A1-replication-prereg.pdf"),
  title = fba_allergy_online_02$specs$T1$text,
  subtitle = "Pre-registration of fba-allergy-online-02 (PRP-QUANT Template, version 4)",
  bibliography = BIB,
  csl = CSL,
  contributors = contributors
)

zpid_state <- prereg_to_zpid(
  fba_allergy_online_02,
  file = file.path(outputs, "A1-replication-prereg-zpid.rds"),
  contributors = contributors,
  bibliography = BIB,
  csl = CSL
)

# The analysis notebook of fba-allergy-online-02 checks these with identical()
# against the provenance record of the data set
write_output(rule_texts, "A1-replication-rules.rds", MANUSCRIPT)
```
